item.title: Do you have seasonal affective disorder? How to tell — and what to do about it
item.description: The syndrome can make people feel like a "hibernating bear," says Dr. Norman Rosenthal, who published the first research on SAD. He explains how to identify the symptoms and what to do to feel better.

item.title: Your writing was flagged as AI. What does that actually mean?
item.description: As editors turn to imperfect AI detection tools to weed out machine-generated submissions, writers who say they were falsely accused of using AI are left wondering what triggered a positive result.

item.title: After last year's storm, this remote Alaska town is still picking up the pieces
item.description: In October, 2025, the remnants of a typhoon seriously damaged Alaska Native villages in the far western part of the state. A year later, one of the hardest hit communities is still recovering.

item.title: 100 years later, Harry Houdini's death still haunts Detroit
item.description: The legacy of magician Harry Houdini still looms large in Detroit 100 years after his death there. Some mark the anniversary of Houdini's death by trying to make contact with his spirit.

item.title: Oyster stocks have plunged in the Chesapeake. This resident wants to bring them back
item.description: Oyster reefs once abounded in the Chesapeake, but overharvesting slashed their populations, leading to poorer water quality and less habitat for other species. Now, researchers and local residents are finding creative ways to bring their numbers back up.
